generalInfo.subHeader: We use this information to calculate costs and applicable incentives.
generalInfo.alertMessage: Anything you share on this tool is used locally for estimation purposes
generalInfo.yearOfOperationTooltip: This number refers to the lifetime of your project, not the term of your financing. The two periods may vary.

workplaceNeeds.resultMessage: This results in a total of 14 vehicles being charged.
workplaceNeeds.subHeader: Let's figure out how many chargers you will need. If you know exactly how many you will need, or you want to overwrite our recommendation, select the charger option. If you aren't sure, we can help you estimate using the spots you have available or the vehicles that need charging at your workplace.
workplaceNeeds.secondaryMessage: Ensure your plans account for an increase in charging needs over time to save on installation. We have provided a “Ports in 5 years” figure which adds a 5% growth in charging needs every year. If you would like to use that number of chargers instead, you can manually input the charger count above.

chargers.label: I know how many charging ports I need

parking.label: I know how many spots I have available

vehicles.label: I know how many vehicles need charging

workplaceNeeds.multipleVehiclesLabel: Multiple vehicles will share charger ports
workplaceNeeds.multipleVehiclesTooltip: Selecting this option if employees will move their vehicles during the day so that multiple EVs can be charged using the same charger. Adds one vehicle per charger to your estimation. We will assume you need fewer chargers, and that you will do management.
workplaceNeeds.chargerUsedForCompanyVehiclesLabel: Chargers will also be used for company vehicles
workplaceNeeds.chargerUsedForCompanyVehiclesTooltip: This will have no impact on number of chargers, but you could have higher electric throughput. Adds one vehicle per charger to your estimation.

chargerSelection.subHeader: Which type of charger works best for your needs? Level 2 is the most common solution, and meets the needs of 90% of projects. Ensure you check the estimated charging times, prices, and outputs in order to choose the best option.
chargerSelection.alertMessage: A generic charger has been selected based on your needs.
chargerSelection.level1Tooltip: Level 1 chargers can be plugged into a standard residential 120-volt (120V) AC outlet.
chargerSelection.level2Tooltip: Level 2 chargers use 240 volts, charge at over triple the speed of a level 1 charger.
chargerSelection.level3Tooltip: Level 3 chargers (or DCFCs) are the fastest EV chargers, and are typically found in commercial or industrial applications. The installation of level 3 chargers is much more complex and expensive than level 1 or 2.
chargerSelection.chargingTime1Tooltip: How long it takes on average to charge a vehicle to 100%. Assuming a <xx> mile commute a typical EV will require <yy:> kWh of charge.A <zz> kW charger will add this charge in <aa> hours and <bb> minutes
chargerSelection.equipPrice1Tooltip: The purchase price of electric vehicle supply equipment (chargers).
chargerSelection.installPrice1Tooltip: The price of installing chargers, including labor, trenching, materials, etc.

siteRequirements.subHeader: We use this information to calculate installation costs. If you select “I don't know”, we will assume you don't need a new panel, but you can always change this later from the assumptions panel.

siteRequirements.needNewPanelTooltip: We estimate an average cost of $6,500 plus sales tax for a new panel. If you select “I don't know” we will assume you don't need a new one, but you can always change this later from the assumptions panel.

welcome.title: Welcome to Charge@Work
welcome.message: Thanks for sharing your charging needs! You have completed the first step, and can now delve through the estimations we’ve generated for your project. Be sure to check out our partners to help facilitate your charger installation project.
